independent_verification.recovered_law: TEXT A presents a solitary speaker addressing a vast, plural, public world (strangers, readers, landscapes, nation) and striking up for a New World outward; TEXT B transforms every relation into an intimate, dyadic bond between 'I' and a single beloved 'you,' turning outward exploration into inward mutual commitment.
independent_verification.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural shift: from an outward, expansive, plural address to an intimate, singular, dyadic bond — moving from sovereign amplitude/catalog to the risk and choice of binding to one particular beloved.
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final lines ('Together, whispering in the near, we begin one difficult life') fully sustain the shifted intimate dyadic relation rather than reverting to the solitary/public orientation of TEXT A.

transforms.source_passage:
Stranger, if you passing meet me and desire to speak to me, why
      should you not speak to me?
  And why should I not speak to you?




Thou Reader

  Thou reader throbbest life and pride and love the same as I,
  Therefore for thee the following chants.




BOOK II


Starting from Paumanok

       1
  Starting from fish-shape Paumanok where I was born,
  Well-begotten, and rais'd by a perfect mother,
  After roaming many lands, lover of populous pavements,
  Dweller in Mannahatta my city, or on southern savannas,
  Or a soldier camp'd or carrying my knapsack and gun, or a miner
      in California,
  Or rude in my home in Dakota's woods, my diet meat, my drink from
      the spring,
  Or withdrawn to muse and meditate in some deep recess,
  Far from the clank of crowds intervals passing rapt and happy,
  Aware of the fresh free giver the flowing Missouri, aware of
      mighty Niagara,
  Aware of the buffalo herds grazing the plains, the hirsute and
      strong-breasted bull,
  Of earth, rocks, Fifth-month flowers experienced, stars, rain, snow,
      my amaze,
  Having studied the mocking-bird's tones and the flight of the
      mountain-hawk,
  And heard at dawn the unrivall'd one, the hermit thrush from the
      swamp-cedars,
  Solitary, singing in the West, I strike up for a New World.
transforms.enantiomorph:
Beloved, if you arriving to stay with me and dare to know me, why
      should you not answer me?
  And why should I not pledge to you?




Thou One

  Thou one tremble with need and fear and want unlike me,
  Therefore for thee this single vow.




BOOK II


Leaving behind the Familiar Hearth

       1
  Leaving behind the familiar hearth where I was safe,
  Unfinished, and taught by a difficult love,
  After searching one face, learner of one threshold,
  Guest in your house not mine, or in your strange country,
  Or a supplicant kneeling or carrying my doubt and my name, or a digger
      in your silence,
  Or awkward at your table, my bread yours, my thirst from
      your well,
  Or drawn close to listen and wait in your difficult quiet,
  Near to the catch of your breath hours passing uncertain and dear,
  Aware of the slow costly gift of your trust, aware of the
      small pulse at your wrist,
  Aware of the one animal warmth beside me, the tender and
      mortal body,
  Of skin, bone, first-night silence endured, tears, heat, shaking,
      my awe,
  Having studied your particular laugh and the tremble of your
      held hand,
  And heard at dawn the only one, your voice from the
      dark room,
  Together, whispering in the near, we begin one difficult life.

kernel.governing_law: The self stands open to all encounter — stranger, reader, continent — declaring that every meeting is already an intimacy waiting to be spoken; the world is a catalog of beloved particulars whose sum authorizes the singer's song.
kernel.mutated_relation: The encounter is not already open but must be won; intimacy is not declared but built — the beloved particular is not cataloged but chosen, and the song arises not from sovereign amplitude but from the risk of binding to one.

independent_verification.recovered_law: TEXT B systematically inverts the relational directions and polarities of TEXT A: life/death, young/old, forward/backward, onward-outward/inward-under, alive/still, birth/unbirth, love/refusal, translation/withholding, and optimism/severity are all reversed, so that every directional flow and causal relation points in the opposite direction.
independent_verification.law_match_note: The recovered claim identifies a systematic inversion of relational directions and polarities (life→death, forward→backward, etc.), which partially overlaps with the declared claim's assertion that life is negated and stillness prevails, but the recovered claim describes a broader structural reversal operation rather than specifically the grammatical illusion/withheld presence framing of the declared claim.
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final ~40% of TEXT B consistently maintains the inverted relational structure (inward/under, suspension, living=rehearsed/sterner) without reverting to TEXT A's affirmative outward momentum.

transforms.source_passage:
Tenderly will I use you curling grass,
  It may be you transpire from the breasts of young men,
  It may be if I had known them I would have loved them,
  It may be you are from old people, or from offspring taken soon out
      of their mothers' laps,
  And here you are the mothers' laps.

  This grass is very dark to be from the white heads of old mothers,
  Darker than the colorless beards of old men,
  Dark to come from under the faint red roofs of mouths.

  O I perceive after all so many uttering tongues,
  And I perceive they do not come from the roofs of mouths for nothing.

  I wish I could translate the hints about the dead young men and women,
  And the hints about old men and mothers, and the offspring taken
      soon out of their laps.

  What do you think has become of the young and old men?
  And what do you think has become of the women and children?

  They are alive and well somewhere,
  The smallest sprout shows there is really no death,
  And if ever there was it led forward life, and does not wait at the
      end to arrest it,
  And ceas'd the moment life appear'd.

  All goes onward and outward, nothing collapses,
  And to die is different from what any one supposed, and luckier.
transforms.enantiomorph:
Warily will I handle you stiffening salt,
  It may be you precipitate from the hollows of old stones,
  It may be if I had forgotten them I would have refused them,
  It may be you are from new arrivals, or from remainders held long in
      the kilns' floors,
  And here you are the kilns' floors.

  This salt is very pale to be from the charred ends of unborn daughters,
  Paler than the vivid rust of children not yet,
  Pale to come from under the hard white seals of throats.

  O I suspect after all so many arrested roots,
  And I suspect they do not come from the seals of throats for nothing.

  I wish I could withhold the omissions about the living things that will not speak,
  And the omissions about children not yet and unborn daughters, and the remainders held long
      in the kilns' floors.

  What do you know has refused to become of the old stones and new arrivals?
  And what do you know has refused to become of the unborn daughters and children not yet?

  They are still and blank nowhere,
  The widest scorch-mark conceals there is really no life,
  And if ever there was it drew backward into pause, and does not begin at the
      start to release it,
  And commenced the moment stillness opened.

  All goes inward and under, everything suspends,
  And to live is identical to what everything rehearsed, and sterner.

kernel.governing_law: The dead are not gone but perpetually expressed through the living substance of the earth; death is a grammatical illusion dissolved by the grass's evidence of continuous transition.
kernel.mutated_relation: The living are not present but perpetually withheld through the inert silence of what refuses to grow; life is the grammatical illusion, and the stillness is the undeceived condition that precedes all utterance.
